ordered_diagnoses: Drug Rash with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute generalized skin eruption with systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Severe generalized bullous and pustular rash
Marked leukocytosis, hyperglycemia, hypoproteinemia, transaminitis, and elevated C-reactive protein level
key_facts: 70-year-old woman with undifferentiated connective tissue disorder and rheumatoid arthritis
Treated with hydroxychloroquine in 2010
Developed severe generalized bullous and pustular rash after starting hydroxychloroquine in 2010
Rash resolved after drug discontinuation and corticosteroid therapy
Hydroxychloroquine was restarted in 2022
Admitted with widespread erythema, desquamation, and pustulation three days after restarting hydroxychloroquine
Denied any history of psoriasis
Laboratory studies revealed marked leukocytosis, hyperglycemia, hypoproteinemia, transaminitis, and elevated C-reactive protein level
Skin biopsies showed separation of the stratum corneum with multifocal subcorneal collections of neutrophils
Underlying spongiotic epidermis with neutrophilic exocytosis, papillary dermal edema, and superficial perivascular and interstitial infiltrate

shortlist: Drug Rash with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms

shortlist.label: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe generalized bullous and pustular rash with widespread erythema and desquamation after hydroxychloroquine restart

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis, with systemic inflammation and skin biopsy findings

shortlist.label: Acute Generalized Exanthematous Pustulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid onset of pustular rash after hydroxychloroquine restart, with laboratory findings of leukocytosis and elevated C-reactive protein

shortlist.label: Drug Rash with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms such as hyperglycemia, hypoproteinemia, and transaminitis, with skin rash and eosinophils on biopsy

shortlist.label: Hydroxychloroquine-Induced Hypersensitivity Reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Previous reaction to hydroxychloroquine in 2010, with similar symptoms recurring after restart in 2022

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including widespread erythema, desquamation, and pustulation, along with laboratory findings of marked leukocytosis and skin biopsies showing subcorneal collections of neutrophils, are consistent with Acute Generalized Exanthematous Pustulosis, a condition often triggered by medications such as hydroxychloroquine.

rejected.label: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
rejected.why: While the patient had a severe skin reaction, the presence of pustulation and the specific biopsy findings are more characteristic of Acute Generalized Exanthematous Pustulosis than Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis.

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
rejected.why: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome typically involves mucous membranes and has a different set of biopsy findings, which do not match the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Drug Rash with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms
rejected.why: Although the patient had a drug reaction, the lack of significant eosinophilia in the laboratory findings and biopsy results makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Hydroxychloroquine-Induced Hypersensitivity Reaction
rejected.why: This is a broader term that could encompass several types of reactions, including Acute Generalized Exanthematous Pustulosis, but the specific details provided point more directly to Acute Generalized Exanthematous Pustulosis as the most accurate diagnosis.
